name: Kubernetes API
description: Direct Kubernetes cluster reads through the apiserver: server version, namespaces, pods and deployments in one namespace, and cluster nodes. Read-only; create, patch, delete, scale, eviction, exec, attach, port-forward, log streaming and the Secret endpoints are all deliberately absent.

tools.name: version
tools.description: Get the Kubernetes version the apiserver reports, including build and platform

tools.name: list_namespaces
tools.description: List the namespaces in the cluster with their phase and creation time

limit.description: Max namespaces to return per chunk (default 20, capped at 50 by this connector)

continue.description: Continue token from a previous response's continue field, to fetch the next chunk

tools.name: list_pods
tools.description: List the pods in one namespace with their phase, node, IP and start time

limit.description: Max pods to return per chunk (default 20, capped at 50 by this connector)

continue.description: Continue token from a previous response's continue field, to fetch the next chunk

tools.name: list_nodes
tools.description: List the cluster nodes with their kubelet version, OS image, capacity and schedulability

limit.description: Max nodes to return per chunk (default 20, capped at 50 by this connector)

continue.description: Continue token from a previous response's continue field, to fetch the next chunk

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.description: List the deployments in one namespace with desired, ready and available replica counts

limit.description: Max deployments to return per chunk (default 20, capped at 50 by this connector)

continue.description: Continue token from a previous response's continue field, to fetch the next chunk

needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED, AND THE DOCS AGREE: Kubernetes authentication (https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/) documents ServiceAccount bearer tokens sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', and the vault entry (integrationTypeRegistry.kubernetes_api) already sends exactly that header in testHeaders. So {type: bearer, field: token} is unchanged, and the test block stays the vault's own testEndpoint, GET /api/v1/namespaces

TLS IS THE LIVE-PROOF BLOCKER, STATED VERBATIM: declarativeRuntime.js issues 'await fetch(url, options)' with only method, headers, signal and body. It sets no TLS agent, no undici dispatcher and no rejectUnauthorized, and it NEVER reads the vault's optional ca_cert field (that field is declared in integrationTypeRegistry but consumed by nothing in the connector runtime). A kube-apiserver on a fresh cluster serves https with a self-signed cluster CA, so Node will reject the connection before any tool runs, with SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN or UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE. There is no per-connector way to skip verification or to trust the cluster CA today. Therefore: these tools CANNOT be live-proven as the runtime stands. The harness must either front the apiserver with a certificate the collector already trusts, or start the collector with NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS pointing at the ephemeral cluster CA, or the runtime must grow support for ca_cert (and an explicit, opt-in insecure flag). The spec is authored anyway, per instruction, and nothing in it is claimed proven

BASE URL IS CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED, SO NOTHING HERE IS PROVABLE BLIND: api_server points at the customer's own apiserver, and there is no vendor-run cluster to shape-prove against. This spec is NOT shape proven by a blind 401 sweep; it is marked for the live harness, which stands up an ephemeral cluster (and a namespace named quoxproof-live where a dedicated namespace is wanted) and drives every tool against it, subject to the TLS blocker above

RBAC DECIDES WHETHER A VALID TOKEN STILL GETS 403: the ServiceAccount needs cluster-scoped list on namespaces and nodes, and get/list on pods and deployments in the target namespace. A namespace-scoped ServiceAccount will authenticate and still be refused on list_namespaces and list_nodes. That is a cluster binding fact, not something the spec can fix

PROBES RESOLVE ON A FRESH CLUSTER, BY CONSTRUCTION: version, list_namespaces and list_nodes need no resource. list_pods and list_deployments probe namespace='default', which exists on every cluster from creation, and both answer 200 with an empty items array when nothing is deployed there, so neither probe depends on a workload existing. The live convention name quoxproof-live is what the provisioner creates when a dedicated namespace is used

LIMIT AND CONTINUE ARE KUBERNETES' OWN CHUNKED LIST: the apiserver treats limit as a hint and returns metadata.continue plus metadata.remainingItemCount when more remains, so every list tool picks those through and accepts a continue token back. The 20 default and 50 cap are this connector's, which is why the input descriptions say so rather than implying an apiserver limit

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE OMISSIONS ARE THE POINT: all five tools are GETs against list and version endpoints. The same apiserver exposes POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE on every resource, subresources /exec, /attach, /portforward, /log, /eviction and /scale, and the Secret and ConfigMap endpoints that would hand back credential material. None is wired here. Nothing in this connector may be described as managing or operating a cluster

CATEGORY CHANGED: the scaffold wrote 'infrastructure', which is NOT one of the twelve values in use in this spec directory (cloud_hosting, commerce_finance, communication, crm_sales, data_ai, developer, files_knowledge, hr_hiring, marketing_email, media, monitoring, project_management). Set to 'cloud_hosting', which is where the other compute control planes live (digitalocean, docker_hub, fly_io style entries). The vault entry says category 'kubernetes', which is a vault grouping, not a spec-directory value

RESPONSE SHAPES COME FROM THE API REFERENCE: picked fields are Info (major, minor, gitVersion, gitCommit, gitTreeState, buildDate, goVersion, compiler, platform), NamespaceList/Namespace (metadata.name, uid, creationTimestamp, status.phase), PodList/Pod (spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, status.phase, podIP, hostIP, startTime), NodeList/Node (spec.unschedulable, spec.podCIDR, status.nodeInfo.*, status.capacity.*) and DeploymentList/Deployment (spec.replicas, spec.strategy.type, status.replicas, readyReplicas, updatedReplicas, availableReplicas, unavailableReplicas). Per-container status, node conditions and addresses are deliberately not picked: they are nested arrays that would dominate the payload. Confirming these field names against a real cluster is the live harness's job
